checks: Substitution into the inside slab leaves the saturated endpoint term affine with slope −Ac and the moving endpoint term −AhJ(κ+t(v−c)/h). The outside slab gives +AhJ(κ−t(v+c)/h), with no remote contribution.

At continuity of Ψ the primitive derivative is W. A stationary primitive argument gives the linear formula even at a jump. The indicated step-CDF example has the two different one-sided first derivatives, so the unrestricted source differentiation is correctly narrowed.

Pointwise differentiability of Ψ at κ gives the second-order Peano expansion by integrating Ψ(κ+s)=W+Ψ′(κ)s+o(|s|). Neighborhood continuity supplies the intermediate first derivatives for the classical second derivative. Both signs match the primitive coefficients.

The affine remote endpoint terms cancel in the centered response. Monotonicity gives convex J, and J−q_+ is uniformly bounded. For bounded κ, applying the positive-part function to hκ±tL proves hD_J→|tL| even when L=0.

The uniform ramp primitive is ((q+1)_+²−q_+²)/2. This gives the claimed two kink expansions and centered value s²/2 at either kink, verified independently for exact rational increments. The formulas are slab identities and do not infer stationarity or minimum status for the underlying facet.
